lines: I have been late to my own birth (two weeks), my own wedding (forty minutes, a record I am proud of), and the funeral of a clock, which is the sort of irony the universe pays for in cash.
I want to meet these people and ask them how.
Leaving earlier is not a plan.
The truth is that time and I have an arrangement in which it takes the shape of a long corridor, and I stop to admire every door.
Did you know that a drawer can be organised?
I did not, until 8:14 this morning.
Last week I finally arrived early to a dentist appointment, and I sat in the waiting room in a daze of unfamiliar virtue.
I looked at the other patients.
They had all, I realised, done this before.
I felt like a tourist in the country of the punctual.
I wanted to ask her how the weather was in the future, but my name was called, and I was, as usual, in the middle of something.
